absent: Destination allocator selection, failure modes, and release callback ownership for bulk and huge migration are not shown.
Page table detachment, data copy, and migration entry install and removal mechanics beyond call boundaries are not shown.
Non huge batch and synchronous migration paths, folio splitting policy, and per mode blocking behavior are not shown.
Zone, node, watermark, control group, and vector accounting definitions and balancing thresholds are not shown.
Event and counter definitions for migration, transparent huge, NUMA, and promotion success are not shown.
Interval tree, file mapping walk, stable tree lifecycle, and fork handling beyond traversal are not shown.
Movable operations driver behavior for offline and compressed pools and isolation flag lifecycle are not shown.
Boot, privilege, capability, and higher level state integration for this memory scope are not shown.

findings.text: Bulk folio migration is offered as a callable service that consumes a source list plus caller supplied allocation and release callbacks with opaque context, a mode, a reason, and an optional success counter, returning a gathered status and leaving unmigrated items in the source list.

A balancing helper migrates a single misplaced folio toward a target node asynchronously under a misplaced reason, restores leftovers on partial failure, accounts balancing and tier promotion events, and reports retriable exhaustion distinctly from success.

A restoration helper drains a list of isolated movable items, routing huge items through a huge path and other items through driver callbacks or least recently used return with isolated accounting reversal.
Huge folio return marks the folio migratable again, queues it on the owning size class active list under lock, and drops a reference.

Successful huge migration transfers accounting and ownership metadata from source to destination, propagates temporary and surplus node status across nodes, and enqueues the destination as migratable active.

Reverse mapping traversal is offered in generic, shared page merging, and migration entry removal forms that visit every mapping of a folio through caller callbacks with filtering and early stop support.
Anonymous group release, stable node lookup, and shared huge mapping write acquisition are exposed for use during migration and teardown.
Bulk migration preserves all permanent failures and unprocessed tail items in caller visible lists while transient split offspring receive a single best effort asynchronous attempt.
Huge folios are attempted before other folios, remain eligible across passes only on retriable outcomes, and unsupported sizes bypass attempt and count as failed.
Anonymous, file, and merged page traversals require the folio to be locked by the caller so that mapping associations and stable tree membership cannot change underneath the walk.
Stable node lookup derives from the mapping pointer with low flag bits cleared and yields nothing for non merged folios.
Anonymous address derivation clamps partially overlapping ranges to the start of the area and signals disjoint or overflowed ranges with a distinct fault value.
Misplaced migration builds a one element list and guarantees it is empty on return, either by success or by explicit restoration of leftovers.
Once a page is marked movable its type identity remains stable until return to the buddy allocator, with offline and compressed pool types selecting distinct operation sets.
Huge active list membership, migratable marking, surplus per node counters, and control group association changes are serialized by an interrupt disabling spin lock.
All anonymous reverse mapping synchronization targets the root object semaphore, with read mode for traversal and write mode for teardown coordination.
Huge move acquires source then destination folio locks before optional anonymous and file mapping locks, releasing in reverse order with mapping locks dropped before folio locks.
Traversals that cannot acquire anonymous locks either report contention for nonblocking callers or block, never skipping synchronization silently.
Shared huge unmapping acquires file mapping protection in write mode before attempting to detach page tables, informing lower layers that protection is already held.
Traversal customization is carried by a control block holding callbacks for per mapping work, validity filtering, completion testing, lock strategy, plus contention output and opaque argument.
Anonymous mapping groups form a hierarchy with a root pointer and reference count, where child release can trigger root release when the last reference drops.
Migration progress is accumulated in counters for succeeded pages, failed pages, transparent huge successes, failures, splits, and generic splits for reporting.

Bulk operation starts with tracing and zeroed accounting, drains huge items, then repeatedly slices bounded batches for mode dependent processing, retries split offspring once, and finally merges leftovers and emits event counts.
Huge attempts iterate bounded passes, accumulating retriable pages for another pass while permanent failures leave the scan immediately and memory exhaustion aborts the whole huge phase.

Huge move progresses through liveness check, destination allocation, ordered locking, subpool validation, unmapping, conditional data transfer, table reconciliation toward success or source, state handover, and destination disposition.

Merged page traversal performs two sweeps distinguishing original versus newly forked membership while anonymous traversal scans a page offset interval across the interval tree with rescheduling points.
Entry expects a populated source list and valid callbacks, tolerates empty input, and guarantees that success count output if requested reflects total pages moved.
Entry expects an isolated folio reference and a valid target node, takes temporary control group and vector context, and never returns with the temporary list occupied.

Memory exhaustion during huge processing fails the current plus already retried pages and returns immediately, subpool folios lacking mapping fail as busy, and transient lock or allocation failures retry rather than drop.

A lone reference indicates concurrent freeing and completes as success, out of range address computation must be treated as fault and not dereferenced, and contended anonymous locks must be observed via the contention flag.
Restoration of driver managed pages warns if movable marking or isolation state is missing, indicating misuse of the putback path.
Freeing requires zero references and coordinates with concurrent read lock attempts by briefly taking the write lock when the root appears locked, requiring sleepable context.
Address translation uses a distinct fault sentinel value to report unmappable offsets, separate from any valid page aligned address.
Migration distinguishes success, retriable, memory exhausted, and permanent busy outcomes as separate observable results that drive retry versus list placement.
